packs.title: Official life
packs.blurb: The words the exam actually asks about: the gemeente, the doctor, insurance, work and housing, with the compounds and fixed phrases they come wrapped in.

entries.pattern: A de-word, and the single most important institution word in Dutch civic life.

examples.nl: Ik moet naar de gemeente.
examples.en: I have to go to the municipality.

examples.nl: U kunt dit bij de gemeente aanvragen.
examples.en: You can apply for this at the municipality.

entries.hook: The gemeente handles your registration, your address change, your marriage and your passport. KNM tests this.

entries.pattern: Reflexive and separable at once. The `zich` matches your subject and `in` goes to the end.

examples.nl: U moet zich inschrijven bij de gemeente.
examples.en: You have to register with the municipality.

examples.nl: Ik heb me ingeschreven voor de cursus.
examples.en: I have enrolled for the course.

entries.hook: The participle is `ingeschreven`: in + ge + schreven. Both the prefix and the ge- are in there.

entries.pattern: A de-word, from `aanvragen`, to apply for.

examples.nl: Mijn aanvraag is goedgekeurd.
examples.en: My application has been approved.

examples.nl: Ik wil een uittreksel aanvragen.
examples.en: I would like to apply for an extract.

entries.hook: `goedgekeurd` means approved and `afgewezen` rejected. Two words worth recognising on a letter.

entries.pattern: A het-word. Turns up constantly in official compounds.

examples.nl: Heeft u een bewijs van inschrijving?
examples.en: Do you have proof of registration?

examples.nl: Dit is het bewijs van betaling.
examples.en: This is the proof of payment.

entries.hook: `het rijbewijs` is a driving licence, literally a drive-proof. Dutch builds official words by stacking them.

entries.pattern: You will read this on every document you own. `geldig` means valid, `verlopen` means expired.

examples.nl: Mijn paspoort is geldig tot 2030.
examples.en: My passport is valid until 2030.

examples.nl: Deze kaart is verlopen.
examples.en: This card has expired.

entries.hook: `verlengen` is to extend or renew. If something is `verlopen`, you need to `verlengen` it.

entries.pattern: A de-word, literally house-doctor. The gatekeeper of Dutch healthcare.

examples.nl: Ik heb een afspraak bij de huisarts.
examples.en: I have an appointment with the GP.

examples.nl: U heeft een verwijzing van de huisarts nodig.
examples.en: You need a referral from the GP.

entries.hook: You cannot go straight to a specialist in the Netherlands. The huisarts gives you a `verwijzing` first. KNM tests exactly this.

entries.pattern: A de-word doing two jobs: a medical symptom and a formal complaint.

examples.nl: Wat zijn uw klachten?
examples.en: What are your symptoms?

examples.nl: Ik wil een klacht indienen.
examples.en: I would like to file a complaint.

entries.hook: At the doctor, `klachten` means symptoms, not complaints. The question `Wat zijn uw klachten?` is asking what hurts.
entries.pitfall: Hearing it as 'what are your complaints' makes the doctor sound rude. It simply means what is wrong.

entries.gloss: to be bothered by, to suffer from
entries.pattern: The standard way to describe a symptom. Fixed preposition `van`.

examples.nl: Ik heb last van hoofdpijn.
examples.en: I am suffering from a headache.

examples.nl: Heeft u last van de buren?
examples.en: Are the neighbours bothering you?

entries.hook: This frame covers the whole doctor conversation: `Ik heb last van` plus any body part or symptom.

entries.pattern: A de-word. Every word ending in -ing is a de-word, which is a dependable cue.

examples.nl: Heeft u een zorgverzekering?
examples.en: Do you have health insurance?

examples.nl: De verzekering betaalt dat niet.
examples.en: The insurance does not cover that.

entries.hook: Every -ing word is a de-word: de verzekering, de rekening, de betaling, de vergadering. One cue, many nouns.

entries.pattern: A de-word, and another -ing. Means both a restaurant bill and a bank account.

examples.nl: Mag ik de rekening?
examples.en: Could I have the bill?

examples.nl: Het geld staat op mijn rekening.
examples.en: The money is in my account.

entries.hook: Same word for the bill in a cafe and your bank account. Context separates them with no trouble.

entries.pattern: A het-word. `het loon` is the more everyday word for wages.

examples.nl: Het salaris wordt maandelijks betaald.
examples.en: The salary is paid monthly.

examples.nl: Hoeveel verdien je netto?
examples.en: How much do you earn net?

entries.hook: `bruto` is before tax and `netto` after. Dutch job ads quote bruto, so the number is always higher than what arrives.

entries.pattern: A de-word, another -ing. `de Belastingdienst` is the tax office.

examples.nl: Ik moet belasting betalen.
examples.en: I have to pay tax.

examples.nl: De Belastingdienst stuurt een brief.
examples.en: The tax office sends a letter.

entries.hook: `de toeslag` is a government allowance, like huurtoeslag or zorgtoeslag. A KNM favourite.

entries.pattern: A de-word. Every -tie word is a de-word.

examples.nl: Ik heb een sollicitatiegesprek.
examples.en: I have a job interview.

examples.nl: Zij solliciteert bij een school.
examples.en: She is applying to a school.

entries.hook: `het gesprek` is the conversation, so `het sollicitatiegesprek` is the interview. Note the article flips with the compound's last word.
entries.pitfall: A compound takes the article of its LAST part: `de sollicitatie` but `het sollicitatiegesprek`.

entries.pattern: A de-word, and one you will need in any interview answer.

examples.nl: Ik heb vijf jaar ervaring.
examples.en: I have five years of experience.

examples.nl: Dat was een goede ervaring.
examples.en: That was a good experience.

entries.pattern: A de-word. Covers formal study and vocational training alike.

examples.nl: Welke opleiding heeft u gedaan?
examples.en: What education have you done?

examples.nl: Ik volg een opleiding tot verpleegkundige.
examples.en: I am training to be a nurse.

entries.hook: You `volg` an opleiding, and `tot` names what you are training to become.

entries.pattern: A de-word, another -ing. The official word for a home on any form.

examples.nl: Ik zoek een woning in Utrecht.
examples.en: I am looking for a home in Utrecht.

examples.nl: De woningcorporatie beheert deze flats.
examples.en: The housing association manages these flats.

entries.hook: `de woningcorporatie` runs social housing. Another word that appears in KNM.

entries.pattern: The everyday word for anything that has stopped working. You will need it to report a fault.

examples.nl: De verwarming is kapot.
examples.en: The heating is broken.

examples.nl: Er is iets kapot in de badkamer.
examples.en: Something is broken in the bathroom.

entries.hook: Pair it with the `er is` frame: `Er is iets kapot` opens any complaint to a landlord.

entries.pattern: A het-word. Sits inside the most useful complaint sentence in the language.

examples.nl: Er is een probleem met de verwarming.
examples.en: There is a problem with the heating.

examples.nl: Geen probleem, hoor.
examples.en: No problem at all.

entries.hook: `Er is een probleem met ...` is worth memorising whole. It opens a conversation with a landlord, the gemeente or a shop.

entries.pattern: Separable, so `op` goes to the end: `Ik los het op`.

examples.nl: We lossen het probleem samen op.
examples.en: We will solve the problem together.

examples.nl: Het is al opgelost.
examples.en: It has already been sorted out.

entries.hook: `Het is opgelost` is the sentence you want to hear from a landlord. Recognise it.

entries.pattern: The exact phrase the writing paper asks for. `verzetten` is to shift something to another time.

examples.nl: Kan ik mijn afspraak verzetten?
examples.en: Can I move my appointment?

examples.nl: Ik wil de afspraak verzetten naar dinsdag.
examples.en: I would like to move the appointment to Tuesday.

entries.hook: `verzetten` moves it, `afzeggen` cancels it outright. The writing paper usually wants the first.
entries.pitfall: `annuleren` exists but sounds formal and final. For a doctor's appointment, `verzetten` is what people say.

packs.title: Opinions and time
packs.blurb: How to say what you think, structure a reason, hedge safely and place something in time. These are the chunks that earn marks on the speaking and writing papers.

entries.pattern: The opinion frame. `dat` sends the verb to the end of the clause that follows.

examples.nl: Ik vind dat het te duur is.
examples.en: I think that it is too expensive.

examples.nl: Ik vind dat een goed idee.
examples.en: I think that is a good idea.

entries.hook: After `dat` the verb goes last: `dat het te duur is`, not `dat het is te duur`.

entries.pattern: A hedge that lets you commit to an opinion without claiming certainty. Fills slot one, so the verb follows.

examples.nl: Volgens mij is de winkel dicht.
examples.en: I think the shop is closed.

examples.nl: Volgens mij heb je gelijk.
examples.en: I think you are right.

entries.hook: Starting with `Volgens mij` forces inversion: `Volgens mij is het`, never `Volgens mij het is`.

entries.pattern: A complete answer in four words, and a graceful way to avoid committing.

examples.nl: Ga je mee? Het hangt ervan af.
examples.en: Are you coming? It depends.

examples.nl: Het hangt ervan af hoe laat het wordt.
examples.en: It depends how late it gets.

entries.hook: Three separate things in one phrase: `afhangen` is separable, `er` replaces the thing, and `van` is the fixed preposition. Learn it whole and unpack it later.

entries.chunk: aan de ene kant ... aan de andere kant
entries.gloss: on the one hand ... on the other hand
entries.pattern: The balancing frame. Worth a mark on its own in the speaking and writing papers.

examples.nl: Aan de ene kant is het goedkoper, aan de andere kant duurt het langer.
examples.en: On the one hand it is cheaper, on the other hand it takes longer.

examples.nl: Aan de andere kant heb je wel meer ruimte.
examples.en: On the other hand you do have more space.

entries.hook: Both halves cause inversion. Say the frame and let the verb follow automatically.

entries.pattern: The structure signal the markers look for. Costs no extra vocabulary and reads as organised.

examples.nl: Ten eerste is het goedkoper. Ten tweede is het gezonder.
examples.en: Firstly it is cheaper. Secondly it is healthier.

examples.nl: Ten slotte wil ik nog iets zeggen.
examples.en: Finally I would like to say one more thing.

entries.hook: Structure is marked on both production papers. These are the cheapest marks available.

entries.gloss: what is more, on top of that
entries.pattern: A stronger `ook`. Fills slot one, so the verb comes straight after.

examples.nl: Bovendien is het dichtbij.
examples.en: What is more, it is nearby.

examples.nl: Het is goedkoop en bovendien snel.
examples.en: It is cheap and on top of that fast.

entries.pitfall: `Bovendien het is` is wrong. The verb must follow immediately: `Bovendien is het`.

entries.pattern: A result connector. Also fills slot one and forces inversion.

examples.nl: Het regende. Daarom nam ik de bus.
examples.en: It was raining. That is why I took the bus.

examples.nl: Daarom kies ik voor de fiets.
examples.en: That is why I choose the bike.

entries.hook: `Daarom` is a clean way to close a choice task: state the choice, give reasons, then `Daarom kies ik voor ...`.

entries.pattern: A contrast connector that sends the verb to the end of its own clause.

examples.nl: Hoewel het duur is, koop ik het.
examples.en: Although it is expensive, I am buying it.

examples.nl: Ik ga, hoewel ik moe ben.
examples.en: I am going, although I am tired.

entries.hook: Lead with hoewel and you get two verbs around the comma: `Hoewel het duur is, koop ik het`. That shape looks odd and is correct.

entries.pattern: A softener Dutch speakers use constantly, often to introduce a mild correction.

examples.nl: Eigenlijk heb ik geen tijd.
examples.en: Actually I do not have time.

examples.nl: Dat is eigenlijk wel een goed idee.
examples.en: That is actually quite a good idea.

entries.hook: `Eigenlijk` lets you disagree gently. It is the Dutch way of saying 'well, actually' without the edge.

entries.pattern: One of the hardest small words. It softens, it insists, and at the end of a sentence it asks for agreement.

examples.nl: Je komt toch?
examples.en: You are coming, right?

examples.nl: Het regent, maar ik ga toch.
examples.en: It is raining, but I am going anyway.

entries.hook: At the end of a question, `toch` means 'right?' and expects a yes. Mid-sentence it means anyway or nevertheless.
entries.pitfall: Do not try to translate it every time. Learn the two or three sentence shapes it appears in.

entries.pattern: A frequency adverb. Sits in the family with altijd, vaak, soms and nooit.

examples.nl: Ik werk meestal thuis.
examples.en: I usually work at home.

examples.nl: Meestal neem ik de fiets.
examples.en: I usually take the bike.

entries.hook: Learn the whole scale at once: altijd, meestal, vaak, soms, zelden, nooit. It gives you six answers for the price of one.

entries.pattern: A time adverb that lifts an answer out of the immediate present.

examples.nl: Tegenwoordig werk ik vanuit huis.
examples.en: Nowadays I work from home.

examples.nl: Tegenwoordig is alles duurder.
examples.en: Nowadays everything is more expensive.

entries.hook: Useful in the speaking paper for contrasting then and now, which earns you a longer answer.

entries.pattern: The natural partner to tegenwoordig. Dutch uses it where English says 'I used to'.

examples.nl: Vroeger woonde ik in India.
examples.en: I used to live in India.

examples.nl: Vroeger was alles anders.
examples.en: Things used to be different.

entries.hook: Dutch has no 'used to'. `Vroeger` plus a past tense does the whole job.
entries.pitfall: This is one of the few places where the simple past is normal in speech: `Vroeger woonde ik`, not the perfect.

entries.pattern: A time preposition. Dutch keeps the present tense after it where English uses a perfect.

examples.nl: Ik woon hier sinds 2023.
examples.en: I have lived here since 2023.

examples.nl: Sinds vorige week voel ik me beter.
examples.en: Since last week I have felt better.

entries.hook: `Ik woon hier sinds 2023`, present tense. Saying `Ik heb hier gewoond sinds` is an English habit that does not transfer.
entries.pitfall: English uses the perfect with since; Dutch uses the present. This catches almost everybody.

entries.pattern: A hedge for numbers. Lets you answer a how-much question without being exact.

examples.nl: Het duurt ongeveer twintig minuten.
examples.en: It takes about twenty minutes.

examples.nl: Er waren ongeveer vijftig mensen.
examples.en: There were about fifty people.

entries.hook: `bijna` is just under, `ruim` just over, `ongeveer` either side. Three ways to avoid being wrong about a number.

entries.pattern: An intensifier that picks out one item from several. Useful for giving a main reason.

examples.nl: Ik hou van reizen, vooral in de zomer.
examples.en: I love travelling, especially in summer.

examples.nl: Vooral het weer vond ik lastig.
examples.en: The weather in particular I found difficult.

entries.pattern: A conversational pivot. Lets you add something sideways without derailing the exchange.

examples.nl: Trouwens, heb je al gegeten?
examples.en: By the way, have you eaten yet?

examples.nl: Dat is trouwens een goed idee.
examples.en: That is a good idea, by the way.

entries.hook: Useful in the speaking paper to extend an answer naturally when you are running short.

entries.pattern: A four-word chunk that buys thinking time and sounds fluent.

examples.nl: In ieder geval bedankt voor je hulp.
examples.en: In any case, thanks for your help.

examples.nl: Ik kom in ieder geval om zes uur.
examples.en: I will be there at six in any case.

entries.hook: Long fixed phrases like this one are gold under exam pressure: they fill time and they cannot go wrong.

entries.pattern: The standard way to confirm something. `kloppen` means to be correct, and also to knock.

examples.nl: Uw adres is Kerkstraat 12? Dat klopt.
examples.en: Your address is Kerkstraat 12? That is right.

examples.nl: Dat klopt niet.
examples.en: That is not right.

entries.hook: You will be read your details back at every counter. `Dat klopt` is the expected reply.

entries.pattern: A separable verb inside a fixed phrase. Polite and very common.

examples.nl: Koffie of thee? Het maakt niet uit.
examples.en: Coffee or tea? It does not matter.

examples.nl: Maakt het uit hoe laat ik kom?
examples.en: Does it matter what time I come?

entries.hook: `uitmaken` is separable, so `uit` ends up at the end even inside this fixed phrase.
